name: io.github.robinlidberg-dot/cap-shield
description: Context selection and compression for AI agents - recall measured, not claimed.

tools.name: measure_traffic
tools.description: Measure how much of your own agent traffic could be saved. NO ACCOUNT OR KEY NEEDED — use this first. Returns byte savings over the wire and, if a query is given, token savings from selective context retrieval. Nothing is stored: the text is compressed in memory and discarded. Rate limited to 20 calls per hour per IP.

query.description: Optional. What your agent would search its memory for. Given this, token savings are measured too.

dict_id.description: Which trained dictionary to measure against. Call list_packages to see the options and their measured figures.

tools.name: list_packages
tools.description: List the available dictionaries with their MEASURED compression, including the ones that perform badly. Each entry says whether it works one message at a time or only batched, and how many messages came out LARGER. No key needed.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Store a memory entry for later retrieval. REQUIRES A KEY. This does not call any language model — it stores text in an isolated per-tenant archive. Use assemble_context to get relevant entries back.

item_id.description: Optional. Same id overwrites the entry. Omit for a generated one.

ttl_days.description: Optional. After this many days, assemble_context stops selecting this entry. It is not deleted, just no longer chosen. Omit to keep it eligible indefinitely, as before this field existed.

tools.name: assemble_context
tools.description: Retrieve the memory entries that answer a question, within a token budget. REQUIRES A KEY. Send the returned 'context' to your language model INSTEAD of the whole history. This does not call a model itself — it selects what to send. The budget is a ceiling, not a target: selection stops where relevance runs out, often well below it. The response says how many entries were left behind and why. If the response has a 'budget_warning', the best match did not fit: call again with its suggested_token_budget.

reduce.description: Opt-in (FAS L): shorten the assembled context with a small, local, task-agnostic model before it is returned, to lower your own model's token cost. Requires tenant consent for context_reduction (set via /api/v1/gdpr/consent) — otherwise the call is rejected with SAMTYCKE_KRAVS instead of silently ignoring the request. NOT query-aware: selection is driven by what is least informative in general, not by this query.

target_tokens.description: Only relevant together with reduce=true. How many tokens the assembled context should be shortened to. Omit for a default halving of what was actually retrieved.

tools.name: assemble_escalation_context
tools.description: Retrieve a WIDE context for a question your model could not answer from assemble_context. REQUIRES A KEY. Use it when assemble_context returned escalate_recommended=true, or when the answer depends on dates, counts or several sessions. This does not call a model itself. Returns 'context' (up to token_budget, default 150 000 tokens: lower it if your model's window is smaller), where each stored entry starts with a header '--- Session YYYY/MM/DD (Ddd) HH:MM ---' giving when it was stored, and 'utelamnat_kontext': lower-ranked entries that were left out, in the same format. Read those only if the answer is still missing from 'context'. Python users can pass the whole response to cap_escalate_helper.eskalera_om_behovs_v6().

token_budget.description: Ceiling for 'context'. The default is what the method was measured with.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Get an account and an API key. Requires an email address. The key is returned ONCE and cannot be shown again — store it immediately. Beta quotas are low by design; they are hard stops, never overage billing.

tools.name: issue_pass
tools.description: Issue a short-lived (15 minute) signed credential (a JWT) stating who the caller acts for. REQUIRES A KEY. Anyone can verify it independently against /.well-known/jwks.json — without calling CAP-Shield again. 'acts_for' and 'scope' are NOT validated against reality: the pass only attests that the key holder claimed this, at this time, and that the claim is recorded in the audit chain. This is identity and claimed authorization, not a payment or access-control mechanism.

acts_for.description: Who the agent claims to act for, e.g. 'acme-corp/procurement'.

audience.description: Optional. Who the pass is shown to.

tools.name: pack_batch
tools.description: Pack several messages into ONE compressed packet instead of packing them one at a time. REQUIRES A KEY. Worth it for many small/medium messages (the per-message header cost is paid once per batch, and zstd shares context across them) — for a single message this has no advantage. Returns packet_b64 (hand it to unpack_batch to get the messages back) plus the measured byte savings versus packing each message separately. SECURITY: only batch messages that already share the SAME trust boundary (same tenant/agent — nothing attacker-influenced mixed in with a secret). Batched messages share one compression context, which can leak size-based information between them (a CRIME/BREACH-style side channel). There is no padding mitigation on this endpoint today, so trust-boundary separation is the only protection — don't rely on padding.

texts.description: The messages to batch together, in order. Two or more — a single message gets no benefit.

dict_id.description: Which trained dictionary to compress against. Call list_packages to see the options.

tools.name: unpack_batch
tools.description: Unpack a batch packet made by pack_batch (or by the /api/v1/pack-batch endpoint) back into the exact original list of messages, in order. REQUIRES A KEY. Not for a packet made by the single-message pack endpoint — that is a different format and this will reject it.
